### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **7** documentable anchor(s).

**9** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/keys (route, a path literal in lifecycleRefusalOf; a path literal in membershipEndedRestoreRefused))_
- `content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/keys (route, a path literal in lifecycleRefusalOf; a path literal in membershipEndedRestoreRefused))_

- `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx`  _(via sys_api_key (symbol, a field of const object arObjects; a field of const object enObjects; a field of const object esESObjects; a field of const object frObjects; a field of const object jaJPObjects; a field of const object ptBRObjects; a field of const object zhCNObjects; a field of const object zhHantObjects))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via sys_api_key (symbol, a field of const object arObjects; a field of const object enObjects; a field of const object esESObjects; a field of const object frObjects; a field of const object jaJPObjects; a field of const object ptBRObjects; a field of const object zhCNObjects; a field of const object zhHantObjects), /api/v1/keys (route, a path literal in lifecycleRefusalOf; a path literal in membershipEndedRestoreRefused))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `PERMISSION_DENIED (literal, 51 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **64** of **227** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **51** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1ff99441d8c5155f14b602181337d43e41ec9b6a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3e344725470e0a5733f387e347769b3f721dc918` — the merge of head `605c353aae51ea09a7cf95fe92d6bacd208ad77b` into base `1ff99441d8c5155f14b602181337d43e41ec9b6a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3e344725470e0a5733f387e347769b3f721dc918 && git checkout 3e344725470e0a5733f387e347769b3f721dc918
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 1ff99441d8c5155f14b602181337d43e41ec9b6a 605c353aae51ea09a7cf95fe92d6bacd208ad77b && git checkout -B drift-repro 1ff99441d8c5155f14b602181337d43e41ec9b6a && git merge --no-ff 605c353aae51ea09a7cf95fe92d6bacd208ad77b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1ff99441d8c5155f14b602181337d43e41ec9b6a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 1ff99441d8c5155f14b602181337d43e41ec9b6a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `a3727aaa72dafd8c1f5bc410495dee173a20cc94`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-api-key.object.ts, the 7 generated `*.objects.generated.ts` translation files, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/action-state-visibility.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/api-key-restore-guard.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/api-key-restore-guard.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/forced-reset-revoke-reason-vocabulary.test.ts, the api-key data-door dogfood test, packages/core/src/security/api-key.ts, the changeset + packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/membership-ended-session.ts (`MEMBERSHIP_ENDED_REVOKE_REASON`, read)

Tier note: the face is a declared widening (one new `sys_api_key.revoked_reason` option), so its tier is `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. The maintainer's standing order of 2026-11-04 pauses that tier for this project, so this record is served at `TIER_DEFAULT` and says so; it is the deviation, not a claim of the higher tier.

### ① Derived judgments

- Widening by exactly one value, `organization_membership_ended`, reusing the framework's own session word (`MEMBERSHIP_ENDED_REVOKE_REASON`, imported, not respelled); the vocabulary pin test now names both values. `admin_password_reset` behaves as before (its tests unchanged and green).
- Restore refusal is server-side, in the restore guard, judged before any standing is read: any user-context un-revoke of a membership-ended key is refused 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` with a message that says why and what to do. System context passes, so a host can re-admit deliberately.
- Reason-only bypass (seat review item): a user-context `{ revoked_reason: null }` write is refused by the ADR-0092 D2 identity write guard, and with that whitelist widened the readonly strip still refuses it; pinned on the engine and on the data door, so the two-step road is closed by two barriers, not by the restore guard alone.
- The caller-facing admission text in `core` gains a membership-ended arm, so a revoked key's caller is no longer told it can be restored.

### ② Semver level

- `patch` on `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/core` under the repo's `fixed` group: accepted. `packages/spec` untouched, `Metadata-protocol: none`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Widening: one more accepted value on a readonly select that only system writes set; existing rows read the same.
- Accepted deviation: platform administrators are refused too (unlike `admin_password_reset`). It is the card's literal ask ("the Restore action refuses a key revoked for that reason"), and an exemption would hand an environment administrator, the restorer cloud#3423 named, the hole back. The admin-exemption variant is measured (exactly the three admin legs and the dogfood admin leg go red).
- Cloud half not in this PR: objectos-runtime's revocation writes the reason only after a pin round carrying this change; the dev's report names the write and two gaps (already-revoked keys are skipped and stay restorable; `banned` carries no reason). The seat files that cloud card.
- PR author `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay write). Not governed (451 lines at round 0).

### ④ Design judgment

- Smallest change that closes the card's hole at the framework seam; ablations: rule removed 5/19 red, admin exemption 3 admin legs red, core text arm 1/23 red.
- Out of scope, carried by the seat: the cloud follow-up above.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-11gi1d`
Reviewed-by: `session_01QUs3BvRcDHXqRU4TSVE4u6`

**VERDICT: PASS**
